status: provisional: the items of the former references/values/*.md moved one to one, each given its depth, the change kinds it is at stake in, a broken_if frame, and its sources; the list is to be re-founded on REVIEW-TECHNIQUES.md (the user, 2026-11-24: "코드 리뷰 기법을 외부에서 찾고, 그것을 바탕으로 재정립해라.")

methods.trace: Requirement-change traceability. Apply rv `~/.agents/skills/rv/SKILL.md`: U0's problem-modeling paragraph and the U3 paragraph on claims against results.
methods.design: Concepts, structure, and quality ceiling. Apply rv `~/.agents/skills/rv/SKILL.md` U2 questions 0, 1, and 2, and the Software Design sections of `~/.agents/skills/python-expert/SKILL.md`.
methods.correctness: Correctness, failure paths, and security. Apply rv `~/.agents/skills/rv/SKILL.md` U3 steps 1-4 and its paragraphs on failure paths and security, and section 4.4.5 of `~/.agents/skills/python-expert/SKILL.md`.
methods.tests: Tests pin the contract. Apply rv `~/.agents/skills/rv/SKILL.md` U3's paragraph on tests, the Software Testing sections of `~/.agents/skills/python-expert/SKILL.md`, and the rule files under the repository's test directories.
methods.layout: Imports, placement, and names. Apply rv `~/.agents/skills/rv/SKILL.md` U1 items 1, 2, 3, 4.5-4.6, and 5.
methods.growth: Size, splitting, and reuse. Apply rv `~/.agents/skills/rv/SKILL.md` U1 items 4.1-4.4 and U3's paragraph on reuse and known implementations.
methods.db: Queries, schema, and storage. Apply rv `~/.agents/skills/rv/SKILL.md` U3 `### DB schema and usage` and the sections DM-Querying, DM-Processing, and DM-Internals of `~/.agents/skills/sql-expert/SKILL.md`.
methods.concurrency: Concurrency, failure, and recovery. Apply `~/.agents/skills/parallel-expert/SKILL.md` (PDC-Coordination: task lifetimes, failure isolation, idempotency and crash recovery) and rv `~/.agents/skills/rv/SKILL.md` U3's tracing of partial completion, retries, and cancellation.
methods.llm: Model calls, prompts, and output contracts. Apply `~/.agents/skills/llm-expert/SKILL.md` sections 2 (structured output and its contract), 4 (diagnosis of bad results), 5 (prompt engineering), and 9 (serving resources and repeated work).
methods.cost: Implementation cost. Apply rv `~/.agents/skills/rv/SKILL.md` U3's paragraph on implementation cost and `~/.agents/skills/prv/references/perspectives/perf.md` items 1-2 and 4-5, read for the code instead of a plan.
methods.docs: Documents and user-facing text. Apply rv `~/.agents/skills/rv/SKILL.md` `### Meaning and organization of documents` and `~/.agents/skills/sucks/SKILL.md` to changed documents, docstrings, and comments.

perspectives.value: Every completion condition and user decision in the requirement copies is produced by changed code or a test.
perspectives.broken_if: a completion condition or user decision of the requirement that no change in the breadth produces

perspectives.applies_when: the requirement copies state a scope, behaviour, error handling, or stored format that the change touches
perspectives.value: No changed line contradicts a requirement or user decision (scope, behaviour, error handling, stored format).
perspectives.broken_if: a changed line whose behaviour is the opposite of, or narrower than, what a quoted requirement or decision states

perspectives.value: The change adds no behaviour the requirements do not ask for.
perspectives.broken_if: a behaviour in the breadth that no requirement sentence or decision asks for

perspectives.value: Every claim in changed comments, docstrings, docs, or test names (always, never, unchanged, keeps) matches the code at the head.
perspectives.broken_if: a changed comment, docstring, document, or test name that claims a behaviour the head code does not have

perspectives.value: Every unit the change introduces or touches (module, class, function, field, status value, prompt, stage) has one sentence that decides membership, found in code, a type, a schema, or a document.
perspectives.broken_if: a unit whose membership sentence cannot be written from code, type, schema, or document: a catch-all field, a list packed into a string, a status with no defined set of values, a function doing several jobs its name does not state

perspectives.value: The change removes the cause of the problem it answers, not only the symptom.
perspectives.broken_if: the cause named from the requirement and the code still produces the problem at the head, and the change only bypasses one of its symptoms

perspectives.value: The change's structure is not worse than a feasible alternative in data flow, state ownership, responsibility placement, and call cost.
perspectives.broken_if: a feasible alternative structure, built from the repository's own parts, that is better in correctness, performance, or simplicity

perspectives.value: Within its structure the change reaches the quality ceiling the structure allows.
perspectives.broken_if: an implementation, prompt, query, or test that falls short of what the same structure allows

perspectives.value: The one fact the change is safe because of holds at its file:line, traced from each input through state ownership, write, failure, and recovery.
perspectives.broken_if: an input and path through the changed code that reaches a wrong value, state, or write, so the safety fact does not hold

perspectives.value: Boundary inputs (empty, None, duplicates, maximum size, unexpected types or enum values) give a defined result on every changed path.
perspectives.broken_if: a boundary input that gives an undefined, wrong, or crashing result on a changed path

perspectives.value: Consumers a symbol search misses (serialized fields, DB columns, wire formats, config keys, flags) still read what the change writes.
perspectives.broken_if: a consumer of a serialized field, column, wire format, key, or flag the change writes or renames that reads it differently or not at all

perspectives.value: Every failure the change adds or touches reaches a caller or a log with input, target, and cause; nothing swallows a failure or replaces it with a default.
perspectives.broken_if: a failure that is swallowed, turned into a default, or reaches the caller or log without its input, target, or cause

perspectives.applies_when: the change handles input from users, files, models, or other services, or builds a query, command, or path from it
perspectives.value: Untrusted input is validated (and bounded) before logic; queries, commands, and paths are built with parameters, never string concatenation.
perspectives.broken_if: untrusted input that reaches logic, memory, or storage before it is validated or bounded, or a query, command, or path concatenated from it

perspectives.value: What the code assumes an external program, service, or library does with what it builds (syntax accepted, shape returned, failure mode) is what that system does at its pinned version.
perspectives.broken_if: a run against a fake built from the system's official documentation, or the documentation itself, shows the system does otherwise than the code assumes
sources: rv U3 steps 2-3 (library source at its pinned version, prove by running)

perspectives.value: Each changed behaviour has a test that would fail on the code before the change.
perspectives.broken_if: a changed behaviour in the breadth that no test observes, or whose only test passes on the code before the change

perspectives.value: Tests observe public behaviour, not private names or internal state.
perspectives.broken_if: a test that asserts a private name, internal state, or call sequence instead of the public behaviour

perspectives.value: Boundary and error paths of the change are covered by tests.
perspectives.broken_if: a boundary or error path of a changed function that no test drives

perspectives.applies_when: the change adds or changes a fake, fixture, or test double, or the real implementation one stands for
perspectives.value: Fakes and fixtures return the same shape as the real implementation they stand for.
perspectives.broken_if: a fake or fixture whose returned shape, nullability, order, or failure differs from the real implementation

perspectives.value: Assertions are exact where the contract is exact; no skip, xfail, or weakened assertion hides a failure.
perspectives.broken_if: a suffix, containment, or truthiness assertion where the contract fixes the whole value, or a skip, xfail, or weakened assertion

perspectives.value: No layer inversion, bypass of a package's public path, private-name import, or import moved into a function to dodge a cycle.
perspectives.broken_if: an import in the breadth that inverts a layer, bypasses a public path, imports a private name, or hides a cycle

perspectives.value: Each new or moved file sits with its concept; no catch-all module, pass-through module, or split used in one place.
perspectives.broken_if: a file placed away from its concept, a catch-all or pass-through module, or a split used in one place

perspectives.value: Names state the responsibility, match the repository's naming and singular/plural, and paired modules are named symmetrically.
perspectives.broken_if: a name that misstates its responsibility, departs from the repository's naming, or breaks a pairing

perspectives.applies_when: the change renames, moves, or deletes a name, file, key, or setting
perspectives.value: No old name is left after a move or rename (docs, tests, patch targets, serialized keys, settings).
perspectives.broken_if: an old name still used in a document, test, patch target, serialized key, or setting

perspectives.applies_when: a changed comment, docstring, or document cites a precedent as grounds (기존과 같다, 관례상, as elsewhere)
perspectives.value: A precedent cited as grounds has a primary record.
perspectives.broken_if: a precedent cited as grounds with no issue, design document, intent-pinning test, or user decision behind it

perspectives.value: What the change adds (files, functions, public names, config keys, tests) is the growth the requirement needs.
perspectives.broken_if: growth in the breadth that the requirement does not need, or deletion candidates the change could take and leaves

perspectives.applies_when: the change adds a new unit: a function, class, method, query, constant, helper expression, or module
perspectives.value: Each new unit reuses an existing implementation in the repository or a known one (standard library, existing dependency, platform feature) where one meets the requirement.
perspectives.broken_if: a new unit that hand-writes what an existing repository function, expression, or known implementation already does
sources: rv U3 reuse and known implementations

perspectives.value: Each new unit has a caller, and old paths the change makes unnecessary are removed.
perspectives.broken_if: a new unit, field, key, or serialized value that nothing reads, or an old path the change makes unnecessary but leaves

perspectives.value: The change bundles no independent purpose (a mechanical refactor mixed with a behaviour change).
perspectives.broken_if: two purposes in the change that can be merged separately with the system still working after the first

perspectives.applies_when: the change adds or changes a database query
perspectives.value: Each added or changed query returns its rows with the fewest conditions that produce them, through the index or structure its access direction can use.
perspectives.broken_if: a query with a condition, join, or scan its rows do not need, or an access direction no index or structure serves

perspectives.applies_when: the change reads or writes a database
perspectives.value: No query per item in a loop where one set query would do; no filtering, aggregation, or sorting in application code that the database could do.
perspectives.broken_if: a query issued per item of a loop, or filtering, aggregation, or sorting of database rows in application code

perspectives.value: Every reader and writer of a stored unit whose meaning changed (across backends, tests, and fakes) is updated.
perspectives.broken_if: a reader, writer, backend, test, or fake of a changed stored unit that the change leaves on the old meaning

perspectives.applies_when: the change reads or writes a database
perspectives.value: NULLs, duplicates, empty sets, and the repository's visibility rules give correct results; transaction boundaries leave no half-done state another session can see.
perspectives.broken_if: a NULL, duplicate, empty set, or visibility case with a wrong result, or a transaction boundary that exposes half-done state

perspectives.applies_when: the change alters a stored format, table, column, type, constraint, index, or data model
perspectives.value: A schema or stored-format change is listed for human review with its compatibility, migration, and rollback risk.
perspectives.broken_if: a schema or stored-format change whose compatibility, migration, backfill, or rollback risk is not stated

perspectives.applies_when: the same work can run twice at once or again (two workers, a retry, a re-sent request, a re-upload)
perspectives.value: Concurrent or repeated runs of the same work end in one defined state, guaranteed by a named lock, unique key, or idempotency key.
perspectives.broken_if: two runs of the same work that can both proceed and leave two records or a mixed state, with no lock, unique key, or idempotency key preventing it
sources: parallel-expert PDC-Coordination idempotency and crash recovery

perspectives.applies_when: the work has several steps with durable state between them
perspectives.value: A crash, timeout, or cancellation between steps leaves a state the recovery path resumes from.
perspectives.broken_if: a crash, timeout, or cancellation point after which no recovery path at a file:line resumes the work
sources: parallel-expert PDC-Coordination task lifetimes and cancellation

perspectives.applies_when: one step must happen before another across tasks, requests, or processes
perspectives.value: Ordering (A before B) is enforced by a mechanism, not by timing.
perspectives.broken_if: an ordering the code relies on that only timing provides

perspectives.applies_when: the change adds or changes a queue, pool, retry, wait, or poll
perspectives.value: Queues, pools, and retries are bounded; nothing waits forever or retries without a limit.
perspectives.broken_if: a queue, pool, wait, or retry without a bound
sources: parallel-expert failure isolation and retry control

perspectives.applies_when: the change adds or changes a prompt, a model call, or the schema of a model's output
perspectives.value: Each changed prompt and its output schema agree: every field the code reads is requested and constrained, and nothing the prompt asks for is ignored by the code.
perspectives.broken_if: a field the code reads that the prompt or schema does not request and constrain, or a requested field the code ignores
sources: llm-expert 2 structured output and its contract

perspectives.applies_when: the change adds or changes a prompt
perspectives.value: The prompt holds no conflicting instructions, and its wording matches the decision the code makes from the output.
perspectives.broken_if: two instructions in one prompt that conflict, or wording that asks for a different decision than the code makes

perspectives.applies_when: the change adds or changes code that reads a model's output
perspectives.value: Invalid, partial, or refused model output has a defined handling path that neither crashes nor silently accepts it.
perspectives.broken_if: an invalid, partial, or refused output that crashes the code or is accepted silently
sources: llm-expert 2 structured output and its contract

perspectives.applies_when: the change adds or changes a prompt, an evaluation set, or a test fixture of model behaviour
perspectives.value: No evaluation answer or test fixture content leaks into a prompt or product code.
perspectives.broken_if: an evaluation answer or fixture content that appears in a prompt or product code

perspectives.applies_when: the change adds or changes model calls
perspectives.value: The number of model calls per unit is the fewest that decide the outcome.
perspectives.broken_if: a model call whose result cannot change the outcome, or several calls where one decides it
sources: llm-expert 9 serving resources and repeated work

perspectives.applies_when: the change adds or changes a computation: a query, aggregation, selection, ranking, search, or numeric routine
perspectives.value: Each computation the change adds or changes uses no algorithm of higher complexity than a known one that meets the same requirement.
perspectives.broken_if: a computation of higher complexity than a known algorithm or platform feature that meets the same requirement

perspectives.value: Each hot path the change adds or changes (per request, document, candidate, row) has the fewest DB round trips, model calls, and network calls per unit.
perspectives.broken_if: a hot path with a round trip, model call, or network call per unit that a batch or one earlier result would remove

perspectives.value: No work grows faster than the input where a dict, set, sort, batch call, or reuse of an earlier result would do.
perspectives.broken_if: a membership test on a list, a nested scan, or a repeated lookup, parse, or call inside a loop

perspectives.applies_when: the change builds a collection or reads a whole body, file, or result set into memory
perspectives.value: No whole data set is built in memory where a streaming pass would do.
perspectives.broken_if: a whole data set, body, or result built in memory where a streaming or bounded pass would do

perspectives.applies_when: a changed passage claims a speed, size, or cost
perspectives.value: Claims of speed in the change are backed by a measurement on realistic data or a proof from the code.
perspectives.broken_if: a speed, size, or cost claim with no measurement conditions and no proof

perspectives.value: Each changed passage is needed for its reader and states the current contract, not history or plans.
perspectives.broken_if: a changed passage that tells history, decisions not taken, or plans (a later version, a pending agreement) instead of the current contract
sources: rv Meaning and organization of documents

perspectives.value: Terms are introduced before use, and the same concept keeps one name.
perspectives.broken_if: a term used before it is introduced, or one concept under two names across the changed passages and code
sources: rv Meaning and organization of documents

perspectives.applies_when: a changed passage gives example values, defaults, or constants
perspectives.value: Example values are marked as examples; defaults and constants are not written as examples.
perspectives.broken_if: an example not marked as one, or a real default or constant written as an example
sources: rv Meaning and organization of documents

perspectives.value: Each claim of a changed passage matches the code at the head.
perspectives.broken_if: a claim of a changed document, message, or docstring that the head code contradicts
sources: rv Meaning and organization of documents
